LESSON: WRITING 11.5.1 SPELLING ANTONYMS, SYNONYMS, AND NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.5: Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to tell the synonyms and antonyms of words? 2. Why is it important to write numbers in words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in words from a selected text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in words correctly in writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the usage of antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in words in effective writing. ● In groups, learners are guided to sign read a text with antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in words from print and non-print sources. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign the antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in words from a selected text . ● In groups, learner is guided to observe a signed dictation of a text with antonyms and synonyms, and write them down. ● In pairs, learners are guided to search for antonyms and synonyms from books in groups, newspapers and the internet, and compile a list. ● In pairs, learners are guided to write a list of antonyms and synonyms and exchange them for assessment. 1. Why is it important to tell the synonyms and antonyms of words? 2. Why is it important to write numbers in words?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: Learner develops the skill of interacting with digital technology as they search for more antonyms and synonyms from

the internet.

● Communication and Collaboration: Learner develops writing skills as they write a list of antonyms and synonyms and, in pairs,

exchange for assessment.

Values:
113

● Unity: is cultivated as learners strive to achieve common goals as search for more examples of antonyms and synonyms in groups.

Link to other subjects

The learner relates the concepts of antonyms, synonyms and writing of numbers to other learning areas such as Kiswahili, Mathematics and

Integrated Science.

Suggested Learning Resources
